writeup: TIC 453692345 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.8146 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 9.71% dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 397.8 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal originates near the target, with a peak signal-to-noise of 25.7 and a centroid offset of 3.2 arcseconds. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine learning screening assigned it a score of 0.55 on the pipeline's likelihood scale. This candidate passed all automated data quality checks.
